subject.title: [Security] CSRF risk via dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback on network-exposed gateway (V-02)

question: Should OpenClaw keep `gateway.controlUi.dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback` as an explicit dangerous operator policy, narrow it with additional browser-origin defenses, or remove it through an upgrade-aware config change?
rationale: The code path is intentional and documented, but it weakens a Gateway browser-origin security boundary; automation should not choose the security-versus-compatibility tradeoff for existing deployments.

options.title: Add narrow hardening first
options.body: Keep the documented flag for now, but add focused defense-in-depth such as fetch-metadata/origin tests and clearer audit guidance without breaking current opt-in deployments.

options.title: Remove or fail-close the flag
options.body: Delete or reject the fallback and require explicit origins or constrained patterns, accepting migration, docs, and upgrade compatibility work.

options.title: Accept current dangerous-mode model
options.body: Document that the flag is operator-owned break-glass policy and close this report after confirming the audit/docs warnings are sufficient.

recommendation.title: Add narrow hardening first
recommendation.body: Keep the documented flag for now, but add focused defense-in-depth such as fetch-metadata/origin tests and clearer audit guidance without breaking current opt-in deployments.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the clearest recent merged history on the adjacent Gateway HTTP origin-auth boundary and can route the security tradeoff with the gateway owners.
